concepts.def: Asymptotic upper bound on the growth rate of an algorithm's runtime or space usage.
Constant time: runtime independent of input size, e.g., array index access.
Logarithmic: runtime grows slowly; binary search is the classic example.
Quasi-linear: typical of efficient comparison sorts like merge sort and heapsort.
Quadratic: bubble, insertion and selection sort; nested loops over the input.
Exponential: brute-force solutions to NP-hard problems such as the travelling salesman.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Big Data — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Big Data brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Big Data.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the complexity of merge sort?
options: O(n)
O(n log n)

mcqs.q: Which describes accessing an array element by index?
options: O(log n)
O(n)

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
options: O(log n).
O(n) - because it searches through items.
Only the root node.
O(1) - because it is fast.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: Any item, randomly.
Only the root node.
The first one added (FIFO).
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: What does in-order traversal of a binary search tree produce?
options: Only the root node.
Any item, randomly.
Nodes in the order they were inserted.
Nodes in ascending sorted order.
